title: Acceptance Canvas: On-Prem Network Request Sprint Lanes and Risk Controls
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Context: We continue to receive high-effort private/VPC/on‑prem requests where network constraints, scheduled upgrades, and air‑gapped environments create ambiguity during intake. Current intake forms produce freeform signals that force manual follow-up, increasing time-to-ship and surfacing late blocking issues during preflight.

Proposal: Ship an 'Acceptance Canvas' — a lightweight, structured intake artifact that captures determinative signals up front (network topology class, egress options, cert/KMS constraints, upgrade cadence, maintenance window flexibility, and a sanitized sample of firewall rules). The Canvas maps signals to an enforcement lane (Fastpass / Standard / Concierge) and enumerates the explicit acceptance criteria each lane requires.

Goals:
- Reduce initial manual engineering triage by 40% for network-constraint requests.
- Surface incompatible configurations at intake so customers can remediate earlier.
- Formalize escalation paths and SLA targets per lane (response window, onboarding runway).

Scope:
- Intake form schema and Console UI surface for Sales/SEs to capture Canvas fields.
- Backend autoscorer that computes a lane suggestion using deterministic heuristics (CIDR breadth, NAT-only, strict egress ban, upgrade cadence <= quarterly, airgap=true).
- Acceptance criteria templates and a per-customer checklist artifact stored in customer record.
- Playbook for concierge lane: dedicated SE engagement steps, proxy bridge patterns, and staged rollout plan.

Key fields captured in Canvas (examples):
- Network topology class: "flat-L2", "NAT-firewalled-subnet", "private-only-no-egress"
- Egress modality: "full-outbound", "proxy-only", "no-egress"
- Allowed ports and sample firewall rule set (sanitized)
- Upgrade window flexibility: "auto-nightly","scheduled-monthly","locked"
- Airgap constraints: boolean + description of pull mechanism allowed
- KMS/HSM constraints and required attestation
- Required logs/audit export endpoints and retention window

Design trade-offs & decisions:
- Heuristics-first approach: start with a deterministic score rather than ML to keep behavior explainable to customers and legal.
- Keep minimal required fields to avoid form fatigue; additional deep-dive fields appear only for high-risk signals.
- Autoscorer will be conservative: prefer sending borderline cases to Standard rather than misclassifying as Fastpass.

Acceptance criteria for lanes (examples):
- Fastpass: customer network provides stable outbound egress to our regional API endpoints on ports 443; documented maintenance window >= 4 hours; KMS not required.
- Standard: customer can allow a limited set of egress IPs, or agrees to use a customer-provided proxy; one-week onboarding runway.
- Concierge: air-gapped or strict KMS/HSM requirements; requires SE-led proxy bridge or on-prem appliance; dedicated runbook and SLA.

Operational changes:
- Console: Add 'Acceptance Canvas' tab in private deployment request flow; buttons to attach Canvas PDF and progress checklist.
- Alerts: Create dashboards for Canvas submissions and lane distributions (fastpass rate, failure modes).
- Playbooks: Update Onboarding Runbook and create Concierge Playbook with escalation matrix.

Metrics / success signals:
- 40% reduction in engineering follow-ups within 7 days of intake.
- Increase in Fastpass rate by 15pp for customers meeting documented criteria.
- Mean time from intake to provision reduced to target thresholds per lane: Fastpass < 48h, Standard < 7d, Concierge < 30d.

Dependencies & integrations:
- Console engineering (UI) PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1298
- Intake backend autoscorer repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deploy-intake/pull/412
- PRD & design artifacts: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/PD/Acceptance+Canvas+PRD
- Security assessment: https://docs.redwood.com/secure/reviews/acceptance-canvas-2026-02

Risks & mitigations: 
- Customers misreporting constraints: mitigate with minimal mandatory verification steps and sample firewall checks.
- Increased SE workload for Concierge lane: build a small dedicated concierge-capacity pool and a rotating on-call schedule for initial 90 days.

Next steps & milestones:
- 2026-02-20: Finalize PRD and heuristics table with Eng & Security.
- 2026-03-05: Deliver frontend prototype and autoscorer MVP.
- 2026-03-18: Pilot with three enterprise customers pending legal/compliance signoff.
- 2026-04-01: Evaluate pilot metrics and iterate; target GA for intake flow in private-2026.04 release.

Stakeholders: Sales Engineering (lead), Platform Eng (intake backend), Console UX, Security, Legal, Customer Success.
